scope: Body prose only; controlled shared-contact comparisons, not consecutive days

readings.label: R1
bestQuotes: Moving that work into a later calendar opening may leave the extra check attached
blockers: The second paragraph restates the scheduling-versus-scope distinction already established in the first.
Expectations, available capacity and a clearer boundary are expressed in a formal administrative register.
The recurrence detail yields some practical meaning but does not supply enough new development.

readings.label: R2
bestQuotes: a note can hold a second idea without promising it those hours.
blockers: Rescheduling, scope, competing projects, chronology and initiative are assembled without a sufficiently clear shared observation.
The chronology sentence interrupts the first paragraph without changing its practical meaning.
Ease of beginning versus capacity to carry expanded work is repeated in adjacent sentences.
The practical-initiative sentence is formal and laborious.

readings.label: R3
bestQuotes: a note can hold the second idea without promising it the rest of the afternoon.
Exploring possible directions and choosing one project to pursue can be separate stages
reservations: The expectations-capacity-boundary sentence remains too formal.
The transition to competing projects is slightly mechanical.
This is an acceptable threshold pass, not an exceptional body.

readings.label: R4
bestQuotes: If the original work already fills the afternoon, the extra check could be left out.
blockers: The central interpretation stacks abstract responsibility, deliberate effort, expectations, capacity and a clearer boundary; that formal register dominates this short body.

readings.label: R5
bestQuotes: a note can hold the second idea without promising it those hours.
blockers: The second paragraph repeats the scheduling-versus-size distinction after the first has already supplied its consequence.
The return detail supplies little further development beyond a conditional earlier-method statement.
The competing-projects idea arrives as an appended option.
The stopping-point, boundary and agreement sentence is procedural and difficult to say naturally.

summary.verdict: Only R3 meets every dimension at 4 or higher. The main packet weaknesses are formal wording, abstract repetition and assembled mini-readings, not counselor politeness or dictated scripts.

limitations: No source fidelity judgment without facts.
No inference about provider identity or causal benefit from a context mode.
No consecutive-day or broader reading coverage established.
